export_partners.name: North America and Central America, nes

insights.title: The biggest trade relationships
insights.text: United States–Mexico $883B; United States–Canada $731B; United States–China $527B. Values are goods traded in both directions in a year.

insights.title: Most lopsided relationship
insights.text: China sells United States $315B more than it buys from it, the largest bilateral surplus among these economies.

insights.title: Whose customer?
insights.text: Among these economies, the US is the #1 export market for 7 (China, Germany, Japan, India, United Kingdom, Canada, Mexico); China is #1 for 4 (Brazil, Russia, South Korea, Australia).

insights.title: Most exposed to one customer
insights.text: Mexico sends 82% of its goods exports to United States. A tariff from that one buyer hits a large part of its export economy.

insights.title: Biggest year-on-year shifts
insights.text: United States's exports to China changed -26% (now $106B), while Australia's exports to United States changed +68% (now $25B). Flows above $20B only.

insights.title: Least and most diversified exporters
insights.text: Russia is the most concentrated: fuels & energy is 67% of its exports (mirror data). United States is the most diversified.

insights.title: What each economy specialises in
insights.text: Sector with the highest share of exports relative to the group average (only sectors ≥5% of its exports): United States: aircraft, ships & rail (2.2×); China: textiles & clothing (2.1×); Germany: vehicles & parts (1.7×); Japan: vehicles & parts (2.1×); India: fuels & energy (2.0×); United Kingdom: gold, gems & jewellery (4.6×); France: aircraft, ships & rail (2.4×); Italy: textiles & clothing (1.7×).

insights.title: What the big economies sell most
insights.text: Across the economies that report, electronics & electrical (15%), machinery & computers (14%) and vehicles & parts (10%) are the largest export sectors.

insights.title: Surplus and deficit champions
insights.text: Largest goods surplus: China ($1.20T). Largest deficit: United States (−$1.33T).

insights.title: The US effective tariff rate
insights.text: US customs duties collected were 6.8% of goods imports in August 2026, up from 2.5% in December 2024. Duties collected in the last 12 months: $311B (+37% on the year before). Refunds to importers were unusually large: $150B in the last 12 months, peaking at $49B in June 2026.

insights.title: Highest and lowest scheduled tariffs
insights.text: By the latest World Bank averages (trade-weighted, applied), Brazil charges the most (7.3%) and Australia the least (1.0%). These averages pre-date the 2025–26 tariff changes.

insights.title: Who relies on trade taxes
insights.text: Taxes on international trade are 5.5% of India's government revenue, the highest here; the median is 1.2%.
